subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Archimedes: The First Engineer
description: A fast breakdown of Archimedes: The First Engineer for builders.

hook.text: A Roman fleet attacked Syracuse. One man's machines held them off for two years.

buildup.text: Archimedes built cranes that lifted ships out of the water and dropped them back upside down.

discovery.text: He discovered the lever principle: give me a place to stand and I will move the Earth.

twist.text: He also invented the Archimedes screw — still used today to pump water in developing countries.

climax.text: When Romans finally breached the walls, a soldier killed Archimedes as he drew circles in the sand.

punchline.text: History's first engineer died doing math.

quiz.question: What did Archimedes' machines do to Roman ships at Syracuse?
options: Set them on fire using focused mirrors
Lifted them out of the water and dropped them
Rammed them with underwater battering devices
